question_text: If ⁿP₇ = 42 · ⁿP₅, then find n.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find n when n P 7 is 42 times n P 5.
insider_note: Dividing the two permutations leaves (n − 5)(n − 6) = 42, two consecutive factors 7 · 6. The larger factor is n − 5, so n = 12 — matching 7 to n − 6 instead gives 13, which fails a one-line check.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Divide and cancel the common factors
steps.margin_note: First mark. ⁿP₇ = n(n − 1)…(n − 6) and ⁿP₅ = n(n − 1)…(n − 4). Their ratio leaves (n − 5)(n − 6).
steps.memory_tip: ⁿP₇ contains ⁿP₅ as its first five factors, so dividing leaves just (n − 5)(n − 6).

recall.must_convey: That dividing n P 7 by n P 5 cancels the first five factors and leaves n minus 5 times n minus 6 equal to 42.
accept: n P seven over n P five is forty two, the first five factors cancel leaving n minus five into n minus six equal forty two
cancel the common factors to get n minus five times n minus six is forty two
the ratio of the permutations is n minus five into n minus six
n P seven by n P five cheste n minus five into n minus six forty two vasthundi
divide both sides by n P five and cancel

steps.why: ⁿP₇ contains ⁿP₅ as its first five factors, so dividing removes everything except the last two factors. That turns a relation between two permutations into a quadratic in n.
common_mistakes: Writing ⁿP₇/ⁿP₅ = 7/5 or 7!/5! — the factorials of r do not appear in ⁿPᵣ.
Leaving (n − 5)(n − 6) as (n − 6)(n − 7) by miscounting the factors.

steps.label: Solve for n
steps.margin_note: Second mark. (n − 5)(n − 6) = 7 · 6, two consecutive numbers, so n − 5 = 7 and n = 12.
steps.memory_tip: 42 = 7 × 6, two consecutive numbers. The LARGER is n − 5, so n = 12, not 13.

recall.must_convey: That 42 is 7 times 6, two consecutive numbers, so n minus 5 = 7 and n = 12.
accept: forty two is seven times six so n minus five is seven and n is twelve
match n minus five with seven to get n twelve
forty two ni seven into six ga rasi n minus five seven, n twelve
solve the quadratic, n is twelve

steps.why: Two consecutive numbers with product 42 are 7 and 6; the other solution of the quadratic, n − 5 = −6, gives n = −1, which is not allowed because n must be at least 7 for ⁿP₇ to exist.
common_mistakes: Taking n − 6 = 7 and answering n = 13; the larger factor is n − 5.
Expanding to n² − 11n − 12 = 0 and keeping the negative root.
